rationale: Base of this submission: the currently promoted leader harness. The deterministic layer, the digest model loop, the closers, the ownership guard, the Dockerfile and the whole test layout are inherited from its tree unchanged except where this submission's note says otherwise.
evidence: the whole submission/ tree against main commit 2f3abb3 (the leader's promoted submission); everything not touched by this submission's diff is its code

rationale: The bed-overflow idea: when place_furniture into the primary dormitory answers no_space, divert the beds to the next dug floor and zone it as a dormitory. First measured by this submission (LT08 pass 0/8 -> 2/8 in its official run). Re-implemented here behind the Overseer's existing idempotence gates, in surge tasks only.
evidence: submission/overseer/harness.py: floor_full(), overflow_site(), overflow_beds() and the divert call in furnish(); the idea and its measured effect are described in a9f894e's public note and goal policies

rationale: Two migrant-wave mechanisms it introduced on top of the same leader base: sizing the bed stock to the wave's peak (SURGE_BEDS=20, beds 42-49 per docs/SEED-FORTS.md) instead of the census, and clamping the model loop's advance_days while the fort is short of beds (so the layer gets daily passes to build and place them).
evidence: submission/overseer/harness.py: SURGE_BEDS and bed_target(), the beds-short branch of closer(); submission/plain/harness.py: advance_cap()'s beds-short clause

rationale: The prompt paragraph telling the model that the deterministic layer owns the migrant-bed chain (ordering, placing, overflow), so the model stops duplicating make_bed work and spends its actions elsewhere. Pattern taken from its note.
evidence: submission/plain/prompt.py, OBSERVATION section, the layer-owns-the-bed-chain sentences (~40 words)
